gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 12 build gate now includes a dedicated libbpf survey checkpoint so this heavy helper consumer stays reviewable beside the existing virtio and storage lanes.

The existing make target keeps the Phase 12 survey tranche runnable through the same bounded entry point the other complex-driver lanes already use, while the focused libbpf-only replay stays separately reviewable through its dedicated build file and checker.
The earlier segment catalog already breaks libbpf into helper-first and high-risk clusters, which is exactly the roadmap discipline Phase 12 requires before any larger libbpf surface widens.
The landed enum-to-name tables provide a proven low-risk libbpf foothold with stable output semantics and no dependency on object loading, verifier interactions, or syscalls.

The landed CPU mask helper now covers bounded string parsing, set-bit counting, the deferred chunk-reader interface for sysfs-style buffered input, and the automatic perf-buffer CPU-budget clamp while keeping the same fixed-width input ceiling that the current libbpf cpu-mask file path uses, so future perf-buffer and feature-probe work can share it without widening into direct file I/O, epoll wiring, or runtime loader behavior.
A dedicated survey gate keeps the roadmap placement explicit now that libbpf helper work started earlier under the tooling tranche but the heavy-consumer rollout still belongs to Phase 12.

The Phase 12 lane should verify that the landed zigux_segments foundations still compile and that the manifest matches which segment files are landed versus still deferred, instead of relying only on older Phase 8 coverage.

The lane needs a current note that explains how the existing helper slices fit into the Phase 12 heavy-helper consumer plan, names the rollback owner and fallback path, records the dedicated libbpf-only replay evidence, and points at one reversible-delivery drill instead of leaving libbpf stranded in older Phase 8 wording.

The landed logging helper keeps libbpf print-level parsing, version reporting, and errno-string glue table-driven and output-stable without widening into environment reads, stderr output, or syscall-backed behavior.
The landed pin-path helper keeps bpffs path joining and dot-sanitization reviewable through bounded buffer APIs before any mkdir, statfs, unlink, or object-loader work enters the lane.

The landed file-path-and-fdinfo helper keeps `/proc/<pid>/fdinfo/<fd>` path construction, bounded map-info text parsing, and the token-preparation recovery split explicit and reviewable before any direct procfs reads, pinned-object reopen flows, token creation, or fd-ownership behavior enters the lane.

The landed reused-map-name chooser and bounded compatibility comparison now keep the DEVMAP readonly-prog exception reviewable in the same helper file without widening into pinned-object reopen flow, fd duplication, or loader parity.

The remaining file-path-and-handle bridge still crosses real procfs reads, bpffs opens, token creation, pinned-object reopen flows, and fd ownership, so the Phase 12 survey should keep that resource boundary explicit even though smaller helper slices already live in the same file.

The remaining cpu-mask-adjacent perf-buffer path still crosses `/sys` cpu-mask reads, online CPU filtering, per-CPU perf-event-array map updates, epoll registration, timeout-driven perf-buffer polling, and the interrupt-routing contract for perf-buffer delivery, so the helper-first parser footing and the newer bounded `perf_buffer__poll()` wait-result bookkeeping helper must stay separate from routing and timing parity.

The shared segment catalog already isolates skeleton population as the nearest post-helper libbpf cluster, but it still depends on `bpf_object`, `bpf_map`, and `bpf_program` model parity that the repo has not started yet.

ELF collection and the surrounding object-loader setup are still the first place libbpf segmentation could collapse into mirror-tree sprawl, so this heavier slice should stay deferred until the helper-first and skeleton-adjacent surfaces are proven.

BTF fixups, extern resolution, relocation recording, and load-time verifier interactions remain the densest libbpf surface, so the Phase 12 survey should keep that boundary explicit instead of blurring it into the broader object-loader bucket.
